answers.answer: Shuffle Factory cards, select players+1 face down and return others unseen; place one encounter token on each of 11 marked territories; randomly select a structure bonus tile and place it face up below Popularity Track. Lowest-numbered Player Mat starts.
answers.evidence: Setup: “number of players + 1”; “without looking”; “11 marked territories”; “Randomly choose one structure bonus tile”; “lowest-numbered Player Mat starts.”

answers.answer: Faction Mat sets starting power and combat-card draw; Player Mat sets starting popularity, coins, and two objective cards. Put character at home base; two workers on the two land-adjoined neighboring territories; four mechs over faction abilities; six stars by faction emblem; six cubes in black-square green boxes; four structures in matching boxes; four recruits in bottom circular spaces; six remaining workers on Produce red rectangles; action token beside Player Mat ready. Leave one-time recruit spaces empty.

You must move the token to a different section, but may take neither action. Rusviet may repeat a section, but each top and bottom action is still at most once that turn. Top-row gains may pay bottom-row costs. Top then bottom is the order; bottom first is forbidden. Costs are all exposed red boxes and must be paid in full first; then take as much or little exposed green benefit as desired. Mat/upgrades determine exact bottom costs and gains.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: “must move”; “full cost”; “top-row gains”; Rusviet restriction.

answers.answer: An enemy worker alone on your structure territory controls that territory and its resources. Enemy units cannot use your structure abilities; you retain those abilities without control, except a Mill cannot produce while uncontrolled. Pay costs from resources on any territories you currently control, even when acting elsewhere.

On normal Move, choose up to two different units, each moving one adjacent territory; one unit cannot use both selections. A transported worker may later move itself or be carried by a later mech move. All units may carry any number of resources; only mechs may carry any number of your workers, never your character.
answers.evidence: Move OR coins; all units bullet.

answers.answer: A Speed-enabled mech entering a territory with enemy workers only stops and cannot move again that turn; enemy workers immediately retreat to their home base, leaving resources. You lose one popularity per worker, down to zero, but insufficient popularity does not stop retreat. Your workers cannot independently enter while enemy workers control it.

Combat happens after all units finish moving, before the bottom-row action; attacker chooses order if multiple combats. Your workers cannot independently move into or out of territory controlled by enemy characters/mechs.

Bolster costs $1: gain two power OR one combat card (before upgrades). If draw deck is empty, shuffle discards to form a new deck; if both are empty, draw none. Trade costs $1: gain any two resources (same/different) OR one popularity (before upgrades); resources go on a controlled territory with at least one worker. Cannot Trade for resources if all workers are at home.

Pay every exposed Produce cost in full before production, then choose up to two different controlled territories before upgrades; each worker there may produce one matching terrain token on that territory. New workers come from Player Mat left to right and enter the producing village. You may decline some/all production. New workers expose costs for future Produce actions, not the cost already paid.

Upgrade costs the number of oil tokens in exposed Upgrade cost boxes; Deploy costs the number of metal tokens in exposed Deploy cost boxes; exact amounts vary by mat/upgrades. Upgrade moves a cube from green box to an empty bracketed red box (not solid-black-bordered), improving a top benefit and reducing a bottom cost. Deploy places a chosen mech on a controlled territory with your worker, never a lake; its ability thereafter applies to your character and all mechs, not workers. Even after completing all upgrades/mechs/structures/recruits, you may pay that bottom action for coins and applicable ongoing recruit bonuses.

Build a structure on a controlled territory with your worker; Factory is allowed, lakes and home bases forbidden. At most one structure total per territory; structures cannot move or be destroyed. A Mill produces only while you control its territory. Mine is your personal tunnel for all your unit movement, including Factory Move, and can be used even when its territory is enemy-controlled.

Put an enlisted recruit permanently on any open one-time bonus space on your Faction Mat; immediately gain two power, two coins, two popularity, or two combat cards. Ongoing bonus corresponds to the circle uncovered where recruit came from on Player Mat: Upgrade=1 power, Deploy=1 coin, Build=1 popularity, Enlist=1 combat card. Resolve active player, then left, then right; stop on game end. In two-player game opponent triggers once.

Both secretly and simultaneously choose dial power from 0 to min(7,current power), and may add up to one combat card per participating character/mech (plus Rusviet People's Army one extra card if any workers present). If both sides have combat mech abilities, attacker uses theirs first, then defender. Reveal simultaneously; add dial and card values; attacker wins ties. Each pays selected dial power from Power Track and discards each played card face-up; card values do not cost track power.

Loser's all characters, mechs and workers retreat to own home base, leaving all resources on battle territory; Nordic Seaworthy can instead retreat eligible units/carried workers to adjacent lakes. Winning attacker loses one popularity per enemy worker forced to retreat, including those carried by defeated mech on lake; winning defender loses none (Polania Camaraderie exception applies). Non-Saxony winner places a combat star if it has zero or one combat stars, none if it already has two; Saxony places after every win while star tokens remain. Loser draws one combat card if it revealed at least one power via dial or cards; zero-total loser draws none.

After all combats, resolve encounter if character remains in token territory; if contested entry is lost, character retreats and token stays. Gains go to encounter territory. Pay printed encounter cost but no normal action costs or mat benefits, including recruit bonuses.

Each player's character, on its first finish of a Move action at Factory (after winning any combat), looks at available Factory cards, chooses one, returns the rest; each player gets at most one permanent card and later visits cannot exchange. Use it as fifth section with optional top then bottom and normal no-repeat rule (Rusviet exception); no matching Player Mat coins, structure bonuses or ongoing recruit bonuses. Factory bottom Move moves one unit up to two territories, or three for character/mech with Speed, subject to normal restrictions; Mine access applies.

Only on your own turn, before or after a top/bottom action, reveal a completed objective; you may wait but must meet all requirements at reveal. Place objective star and put both objective cards at bottom of deck. Normally only one objective star; Saxony retains second card and may score both.

Stars for six upgrades, four mechs, four structures, four recruits, all eight workers on board, one revealed completed objective, combat victory (up to two stars), 18 popularity, or 16 power. Each goal once except two combat stars and Saxony exception. Stars are permanent even if power/popularity drops; other players' stars do not block a goal. Sixth star ends play immediately, with no equalizing turns or further actions.

If bottom action earns sixth star, collect primary benefit, coins, and your ongoing recruit benefit before placing star. Unresolved intermingled battle: undo that part of movement, returning initiating units to origin; do not resolve another combat. For neighbor power/popularity recruit stars, finish active action, resolve active player then left then right and check game end at each; if sixth star already placed, later recruit star/bonus does not resolve.

At popularity 10 (tier 7–12), 5 stars add $20; four normal territories plus Factory count as 7 locations (Factory counts 3), adding $21; 13 resources make 6 complete pairs, adding $12. Add those $53 to held coins and selected structure bonus. Structure bonus is scored from your structures even when enemies control their territories. Tiebreakers: workers+mechs+structures (not character), power, popularity, controlled resources, controlled territories, stars placed.

Home base is not a territory and normally cannot be entered, built on, or deployed on; setup and forced retreats are exceptions, as is Crimea Wayfare when unlocked. Two bases without matching core factions are inactive expansion placeholders.
Mountain→metal, tundra→oil, farm→food, forest→wood, village→worker; lake and Factory produce nothing. Workers are not resources. Resource supply has no limit; use multipliers if needed.

All units may pick up, carry and drop any number of resources during movement; mechs can carry workers but never character. Speed adds one territory to each selected character/mech, not workers. Tunnel jump costs one step; extra Speed step may be before or after. Stops for enemy units/character encounters override Speed.
Any unit may enter an enemy-structure-only territory and take control without combat. All printed tunnel territories are adjacent for movement by any unit.
Never pay a partial cost. If unable to afford any action, take a dead turn: move token to a different section and take neither action. Since last used Move, choose any different section.

Armory grants +1 power on Trade; Monument grants +1 popularity on Bolster. These are built-structure benefits for corresponding future actions. You retain structure abilities even without control, except Mill production; enemy units do not gain your structure abilities.

Riverwalk is an unlockable mech ability for all factions, including Nordic; it lets character and all mechs cross rivers onto faction-specific terrain: Nordic/Saxony forests and mountains; Rusviet farms and villages; Crimea farms and tundra; Polania villages and mountains. It does not apply to workers. Nordic Swim is a separate starting ability for workers to cross rivers to land terrain, not lakes; it does not grant mech movement.

Saxony Underpass: controlled mountains and all tunnels, including own Mine, are adjacent for character/mech Move. Rusviet Township: controlled villages and Factory are adjacent for character/mech Move. Workers cannot use these shortcuts.

Saxony Disarm applies before combat on a tunnel or own Mine: opponent loses two power on track, once per combat, not per unit. Nordic Artillery may be used before combat by paying one power to reduce opponent's power by two, once per combat, not per unit.
Rusviet People's Army adds one card total in combat if at least one worker is present; two mechs and three workers therefore allow three cards (two for mechs, plus one). Workers alone never fight.

Crimea Wayfare lets character/mechs move from a territory or home base to your own or any inactive faction home base regardless of distance, including inactive expansion bases. Cannot enter an active opponent's base.

Crimea Scout, before combat, steals one random opponent combat card into your hand, once per combat, not per unit. Starting Coercion lets you spend one combat card once per turn as any one resource regardless of card value.

Nordic Seaworthy lets character/mechs move to/from lakes and retreat to an adjacent lake instead of home; Polania Submerge lets character/mechs move to/from lakes and from any lake to any other lake, with no adjacent-lake retreat exception. With either ability, workers on lakes need a mech to move off; cannot leave carried workers or resources behind on lake when carrier leaves.

Polania Camaraderie prevents popularity loss for opposing workers forced to retreat after you win combat as aggressor on your turn. It does not cover popularity loss for driving off undefended workers without combat.

Polania may choose up to two different options on one encounter card, in either order; first gain may pay second cost. Must pay printed cost for each chosen option, and may take as little of benefit as desired.
In Factory bottom Move, a character reaching encounter territory stops and cannot move again that turn; resolve encounter after whole Move action and all combats, if character remains there.

Coins are not hidden information, but exact total need not be disclosed when asked. Combat-card hand count is public; during combat you may conceal whether you committed cards until reveal, and card contents are secret until revealed. Objective contents are secret until completed and revealed.

Only coins are tangible items exchangeable; agreements are informal and unenforceable (tournament play forbids even coin exchanges for deals/alliances). Payment cannot cancel combat after movement has initiated it; combat resolves after Move, though bribes may influence outcome.

Popularity 0–6: each star $3, each territory count $2, each pair resources $1. Popularity 7–12: $4, $3, $2. Popularity 13–18: $5, $4, $3. Controlled lakes count; home bases do not. Only complete resource pairs score; leftover single ignored.

Count each unique qualifying feature across all structures; rivers do not break adjacency. Encounters count by printed location even when token removed; Mines are not printed tunnels. Payouts for each tile: 1 feature $2; 2–3 $4; 4–5 $6; 6 $9 for tunnels and 6–7 $9 for lakes or encounters; zero scores zero.

Structures on tunnels: printed tunnel territories (not Mines), 1=$2, 2=$4, 3–4=$6. Structures in a row: only longest continuous straight line, rivers do not break it; 1=$2, 2=$4, 3=$6, 4=$9. Structures on farms/tundras: combined qualifying structures; 1=$2, 2=$4, 3=$6, 4=$9.
Yes. Winning attacker loses one popularity for each enemy worker forced to retreat, including workers carried by a defeated mech on a lake.

No. Star placement is permanent, but current popularity may later drop and determines final scoring. The summary says other players' stars do not block a goal, so two factions may each earn a star for the same achievement.

Deal one Faction Mat and one Player Mat randomly to each player. Seat factions in board order: Nordic, Rusviet, Crimea, Saxony, Polania clockwise, omitting inactive factions. Relative seating matters because ongoing recruit bonuses trigger for immediate left/right neighbors.

River is a border between two land territories; lake occupies an entire hex and extends to every adjacent shoreline. A unit with applicable lake ability may enter from any surrounding land territory adjoining those shores.
No. Show encounter card to all when drawn, show its artwork, and read capitalized thematic text aloud; options need not all be read aloud.
No limit applies to friendly units or resource tokens on a territory.

After current player starts a noninteractive bottom-row action, next clockwise player may begin their turn while current player decides which upgrade, mech, structure, or recruit to gain. Resolve interactive bonuses and game-end priority in order.
No. Top action once and bottom action once per turn; actions are limited to once within a turn even for Rusviet, though Rusviet may repeat a section. Costs paid once for action taken.
Normal Move alternative is gain $1 instead of moving.
No. Workers never return to Player Mat; producing workers come from Player Mat left to right. Retreat sends workers to home base, not Player Mat.
Yes. You may attack with zero power/popularity.
Yes. May still fight after reaching combat-star limit; non-Saxony places no further combat stars after two.
Must choose one affordable option if faction lacks Meander; cannot choose unaffordable coin/popularity option. Must pay printed cost but may take as little of chosen benefit as desired.
No: both combatants simultaneously and secretly select dial and optional cards. Reveal simultaneously after both choose.
Announce the bottom-row action so neighbors can check recruit bonuses.

Star goals are placed as soon as achieved; stars are permanent and sixth immediately ends game, so you cannot delay/decline. Completed objective is different: may wait to reveal, but must meet all requirements at moment of reveal, and objective star occurs on reveal.
Normally units cannot cross rivers or enter lakes; faction/mech abilities provide exceptions.
No. Recruit is placed permanently on any open one-time recruit bonus on Faction Mat and cannot later move.
No. Only character triggers encounter; entering with a character stops movement and token is resolved after Move and combats if character remains.

While you control Mill territory, it provides one bonus production territory in addition to normal allowance (two→up to three, upgraded three→up to four). Mill counts as one producing worker; each actual worker there also produces normally, so Mill output is added. Mill produces by terrain even without actual worker.
Control a territory by having a unit there, or your structure there with no enemy unit. Resources alone do not establish/preserve control; leaving last unit with no structure means no stated control.
Build uses wood; Enlist uses food.
